title: Radius-Aware Risk Certificates for Switchback Experiments with Polynomially Decaying Carryover
banked_reason: The advertised all-policy frontier remains conditional on the unresolved sequential multiscale certificate; D0.5 graded the sound delivered package incremental with paper_score_ceiling 4.3 below the field floor 7.2.
gap_reasons: The advertised polynomial-memory oracle frontier is not delivered: the note proves only the Markov truncated-HT upper bound, while its all-policy lower bound is assumed in a conditional theorem.
The horizon-eight cancellation and endpoint calculations do not control general assignment paths and therefore contribute no asymptotic converse.
Because the note supplies neither an unconditional logarithmic lower bracket nor policy-optimality evidence, its contribution and leading-journal significance remain well below the field-tier target.
proof_attempt_summary: The run audited and strengthened the constructive Markov/truncated-HT side, proving a radius-aware optimized upper certificate and preserving the ordinary no-carryover boundary. It repaired the adaptive-likelihood typing, built randomized-offset block and arm-specific band priors, and proved their local posterior-variance, endpoint-separation, and divergence calculations. The all-policy lower frontier nevertheless remained conditional: the attempted first-separating-node/dyadic charging argument did not yield a common-measure occupancy-information inequality, and an explicit T=16 path refuted its naive single-threshold form.
tldr: The constructive side is now an exact finite-horizon radius-aware certificate: optimize the audited Markov truncated Horvitz--Thompson bound over integer windows and cap it by the zero estimator's \(4B^2\) risk.  The certified window is constant when \(C/B\) is below the \(T^{-1/2}\) elbow, has scale \(\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\) in the intermediate regime, and saturates at the horizon when \(C/B\) reaches order \(T^\beta\).  The policy-uniform converse remains open: the common-null calculations do not yet prove even the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) multiscale certificate, so the displayed matched frontier is explicitly conditional.  The \(C=0\) boundary retains the ordinary parametric frontier.
gap: Finite-order minimax switchback theory, geometric-mixing analyses, and recent sequential rerandomization do not supply a policy-uniform common-null information certificate for fixed-array polynomial memory. The banked predecessor already supplies the oracle upper architecture but leaves its lower bound at the no-carryover rate because its two cadence certificates are not complementary.
fill: The project makes the common-null sequential multiscale certificate the single new solve target, anchored by an explicit horizon-eight block-and-band likelihood calculation. The inherited Markov upper bound, no-memory boundary, and operational window are audited supporting results; they become a matched frontier only through the new certificate.
